title: Open compact-support exchange is the extension-composition mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Work on the small etale sites with the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. All schemes mentioned are Noetherian [def-pc-scheme]. Compact-support direct image is the compactification-independent functor of [def-amb-etale-compact-support, lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Let $f:X\to S$ be separated finite type and compactifiable [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $u:U\hookrightarrow S$ be open, and put $X_U=X\times_SU$, $v:X_U\hookrightarrow X$, and $f_U:X_U\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use termwise open extension $Du_!,Dv_!$ with the sum/evaluation adjunctions $Du_!\dashv u^*$, $Dv_!\dashv v^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Identify compact support along an open $w$ with $Dw_!$ using the compactification $(w,\mathrm{id})$ and the refinement comparisons of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Under this normalized identification, let
$$\delta_M:Rf_!Dv_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Du_!Rf_{U!}M$$
be $\alpha_{u,f_U}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{f,v}$, for the composition comparisons of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] and $fv=uf_U$. Let $C_{f,u,F}:u^*Rf_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{U!}v^*F$ be the canonical compact-support exchange. For every $F\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the morphism
$$\kappa_F=Rf_!(\varepsilon_{v,F})\circ\delta_{v^*F}^{-1}:Du_!Rf_{U!}v^*F\longrightarrow Rf_!F$$
has adjunct $C_{f,u,F}^{-1}$ under $Du_!\dashv u^*$. Equivalently,
$$\kappa_F=\varepsilon_{u,Rf_!F}\circ Du_!(C_{f,u,F}^{-1}).$$
Here $\varepsilon_u,\varepsilon_v$ are the evaluation counits. Thus the right-adjoint restriction isomorphism obtained by the Hom chain through $Dv_!$, $\delta$, and $Du_!$ is paired with this specific exchange $C_{f,u}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. No boundedness assumption on $F$ is made.

proof.text: Choose a compactification $f=rj$ and its pullback along $u$, writing $b:\overline X_U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $j_U:X_U\hookrightarrow\overline X_U$ and $r_U:\overline X_U\to U$. Put $J=Dj_!$, $J'=Dj_{U!}$, $V=Dv_!$, $B=Db_!$, $L=Du_!$, $P=Rr_*$ and $P'=Rr_{U*}$. Let $a:JV\xrightarrow{\sim}BJ'$ be the open composition identification for $jv=bj_U$, with its adjunction normalization [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. Open compact support is identified with termwise open extension by choosing $(w,\mathrm{id})$; the candidate is literally $R\mathrm{id}_*Dw_!\cong Dw_!$, and the compact-support comparison theorem identifies any other choice with this one. No comparison for general etale morphisms is needed. The sheaf counit for an open is evaluation [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], and its termwise derived adjunction is [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Let $\Gamma:LP'\xrightarrow{\sim}PB$ be the interchange for the cartesian square $(b,r_U,r,u)$. The specified tower formula for $\alpha$ gives $\delta_M^{-1}=P(a_M^{-1})\circ\Gamma_{J'M}$: for $\alpha_{f,v}$ the tower square has identity bottom open and gives the open composition identification, while for $\alpha_{u,f_U}$ it is precisely the square $(b,r_U,r,u)$. Thus this equality uses the specified composition comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms. All schemes here are Noetherian by the standing convention; the open maps are quasi-compact and finite type since their targets are Noetherian. Properness and the given compactification supply compactifications of $f_U$ and $fv$. The comparison and interchange statements therefore apply on the whole unbounded categories.

Here is the mate calculation with all maps specified. Write $E:u^*P\to P'b^*$ for proper exchange and $e:b^*J\xrightarrow{\sim}J'v^*$ for the inverse open base-change comparison. Then $C_F=P'(e_F)\circ E_{JF}$ by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. The open comparison has the unit normalization of [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility]; its degreewise equality descends to complexes. For $H=J'v^*F$ define $h=J(\varepsilon_{v,F})\circ a_{v^*F}^{-1}:BH\to JF$. The sheaf evaluation counit, the adjunction-normalized open composition map $a$, and the unit-normalized comparison $e$ give
$$e_F\circ b^*h\circ\eta_{b,H}=1_H.$$
Indeed, on an etale test object over $\overline X_U$, both $b^*BH$ and $H$ are extension by zero from $X_U$. Restricting to $X_U$ identifies $a$ with the identity composition comparison, the restricted evaluation counit with the identity by the open triangle identity, and $e$ with the identity by its unit normalization. Equivalently this is the equality of maps from an open extension determined by their adjoints; the sheaf adjunction formula proves it before passage to complexes. Naturality makes the equality degreewise compatible with differentials, hence an equality in the derived category.

The cartesian clause of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] says that the adjunct of $\Gamma_H$ is $\lambda_H^{-1}$, where $\lambda_H=P'(\eta_{b,H}^{-1})\circ E_{BH}$. Consequently
$$E_{BH}\circ u^*(\Gamma_H)\circ\eta_{u,P'H}=P'(\eta_{b,H}).$$
By Step 1, $\kappa_F=P(h)\circ\Gamma_H$. For its adjunct $m_F=u^*\kappa_F\circ\eta_{u,P'H}$, naturality of $E$ with respect to $h$ now gives the fully typed calculation
$$\begin{aligned}
C_F\circ m_F
&=P'(e_F)\circ E_{JF}\circ u^*P(h)\circ u^*(\Gamma_H)\circ\eta_{u,P'H}\\
&=P'(e_F\circ b^*h)\circ E_{BH}\circ u^*(\Gamma_H)\circ\eta_{u,P'H}\\
&=P'(e_F\circ b^*h\circ\eta_{b,H})=1_{P'H}.
\end{aligned}$$
Since $C_F$ is an isomorphism, $m_F=C_F^{-1}$. This calculation also fixes the inverse order: $C_F^{-1}=E_{JF}^{-1}\circ P'(e_F^{-1})$.

proof.text: The adjunction bijection for $Du_!\dashv u^*$ is injective. Therefore the equality of adjuncts in Step 2 proves $\kappa_F=\varepsilon_{u,Rf_!F}\circ Du_!(C_{f,u,F}^{-1})$. Every cited comparison and adjunction is constructed on the whole ordinary unbounded derived category, so the argument applies to arbitrary $F$ and uses no boundedness hypothesis.
